title: RIKEN and Quantinuum Demonstrate Heterogeneous Multi-QPU Workflows on Fugaku - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quantinuum, University of Tsukuba and RIKEN R-CCS linked Fugaku simultaneously to two physically separate QPUs (IBM Heron R2 ibm_kobe and Quantinuum Reimei trapped-ion) via an HPC-extended Tierkreis workflow, using superconducting VQE to warm-start trapped-ion QPE and cutting ground-state energy error roughly fourfold versus standalone VQE.

insights.claim: Quantinuum, the University of Tsukuba and RIKEN R-CCS demonstrated the first multi-modality quantum-classical workflow linking the Fugaku supercomputer simultaneously to two geographically separated QPUs: the on-site 156-qubit IBM Heron R2 ibm_kobe and the 20-qubit Quantinuum Reimei trapped-ion system at Wako (~500 km away).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals that HPC centers are positioning as vendor-neutral orchestrators of multiple QPU vendors rather than single-vendor buyers.
insights.locator: Researchers from Quantinuum, the University of Tsukuba

insights.claim: Quantinuum's open-source Tierkreis dataflow framework was extended with executors for Fugaku's native pjsub scheduler and direct sqcsub quantum submission, bypassing commercial cloud queues and dispatching QPU tasks over low-latency gRPC services.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Workflow middleware that integrates natively with supercomputer schedulers is a software moat for Quantinuum in on-prem HPC-quantum deals.

insights.claim: Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms commonly rely on fragmented glue code, bash scripts and manual job handling that fail to scale in production supercomputing environments, which is the problem formal DAG-based orchestration targets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Orchestration tooling is a bottleneck to production hybrid quantum use; watch adoption of standardized workflow layers.

insights.claim: Heterogeneous quantum chemistry and condensed-matter workflows can run across different quantum hardware architectures without physical quantum interconnects, using classical supercomputers as the central orchestrator.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reduces near-term dependence on quantum networking for multi-QPU value; favors HPC integrators.

insights.claim: In the Fugaku demo, the fast superconducting ibm_kobe processor ran 500 VQE iterations (SPSA optimizer, 20,000 shots per circuit) on a 16-site 2D transverse-field Ising model, then passed parameters classically to seed a deep Trotterized QPE run on trapped-ion Reimei (300 shots, with leakage-detection gadgets).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows a division of labor: superconducting for high-repetition optimization, trapped-ion for deep high-fidelity circuits — suggests complementary rather than winner-take-all modalities.

insights.claim: Warm-starting trapped-ion phase estimation with superconducting VQE reduced ground-state energy error to (E − Eexact)/J = 0.61 ± 0.36, versus 2.47 ± 0.10 for standalone VQE on ibm_kobe and 3.45 for a classically optimized product-state baseline.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A concrete hardware result favoring hybrid multi-vendor pipelines over single-modality execution.

insights.claim: A second case study re-ran Fugaku-driven biomolecular excited-state workflows (subtractive ONIOM and TE-QSCI) and found Tierkreis automated 80% of runtime coordination across the NTChem classical chemistry package and quantum circuit generation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantifies operational labor savings from workflow automation in quantum chemistry pipelines.
